chapter_theme: The fire rite (அக்கினி காரியம்): the Brahmins' oblation sustains sky, earth and gods and burns away deeds, and the Lord is within the sacrificial fire as the light in the heart.
structure_note: 214 to 220 speak of the outer rite and its fruits, with 216 to 218 turning toward an inner fire; 221 to 223 identify the fire with the Lord.

214.reading: If steadfast Brahmins learned in the Veda pour the oblation, sky and earth, the quarters and the gods who rule them, and blameless great wealth all flourish.
214.nuance: The verse makes the rite a support of the whole world. விசையும் in the third line is unclear to me; it may be 'force' or 'speed'.

215.reading: The Brahmins who make the oblation seek the higher way, give to others before they eat, and reach the true path that the rule asks of them by their own understanding.
215.nuance: புறங்கொடுத்து உண்ணுவர can be 'eat after giving to others' or 'turn their backs and eat'; போகதி is unclear. I take the first reading, but it is a choice.

216.reading: For the Brahmins, the fire within the fire, and the inner meaning set within it, become, when it moves in the paired hours, a pure path that supports them.
216.nuance: அங்கியுள் அங்கி, the fire within the fire, is taken as an inner fire matching the outer one of the rite. இணைதுணை யாமம் may be the paired twilights or the paired breaths. I can't fix the sense.

217.reading: The verse speaks of reciting at two times and doing grace, of two that stand together in delight, and of cool birds that are two and grow heady; its sense is unclear.
217.nuance: Every line turns on 'two' (இரண்டு). Pairs like the two breaths, the two daily rites or Siva and Sakti are possible keys, but the verse doesn't name one, and I won't choose.

218.reading: For those who know how the tall flame fed by ghee reaches and burns the darkness, the darkness loosens that very day; and the wealth that lies in deeds becomes fire.
218.nuance: மை can be soot, darkness or blackness of the self; taken as impurity, the flame of the rite burns the soul's dark. The last line may mean that wealth gained by deeds is fuel for the fire or that it is itself harmful (தீயது, 'fire' or 'evil').

219.reading: As the wick laid in a wide lamp burns, the many ills of deeds lasting through ages fall away when the fire is worshipped and rises; the fire burns up deeds.
219.nuance: Deeds are called diseases (வினை நோய்), and the fire is their cure. வீழிசெய்து in the last line is obscure.

220.reading: Knowing great wealth to be ruin, they seek the Lord who made and gave the wealth to come, and, reckoning on the joy it will bring, they keep to the oblation, the rare wealth.
220.nuance: The verse sets two wealths against each other: the great wealth (பெருஞ்செல்வம்) that ruins and the rare wealth (அருஞ்செல்வம்) of the rite. Which wealth 'the wealth to come' is, worldly or the joy beyond, isn't clear.

221.reading: The Lord who is bright flame and without end, who as that flame dwells in my heart, the light in the eye who passes beyond the seven worlds, is also the cool flame that heads the fire offering.
221.nuance: The verse joins three lights: the flame of the rite, the flame in the heart, and the light that passes beyond the worlds. 'Cool flame' (தண்சுடர்) is a deliberate paradox.

222.reading: Our Lord is in the fire of the oblation, and in the fire of the funeral pyre as the one who takes its essence; another fire yields the sea of deeds, and another is the roaring sea itself.
222.nuance: Four fires are named: ஓமம் (the rite), ஈமம் (the pyre), வேமம் and கோமம். The last two are obscure; கோமம் with the roaring sea may be the fire under the sea of Tamil tradition. My reading of lines 3 and 4 is a guess.

223.reading: The austere ones who tend the fire, who granted the way of abiding in the Veda, set it everywhere; and the great Lord, rising, establishes them: that is their glory.
223.nuance: The subject of the second half is unclear: the Lord may establish the fire or the ascetics. இளைப்ப is obscure.

links.note: Tirumular praises the oblation as sustaining sky, earth and gods; the Kural ranks not killing above a thousand oblations. Read together, the rite keeps its worth but not the first place.
If புறங்கொடுத்து உண்ணுவர means eating after giving, both describe the worthy as feeding others first and eating after.

220 says those who know great wealth to be ruin (பெருஞ்செல்வம் கேடென்று) keep to the oblation as the rare wealth (அருஞ்செல்வத்து ஆகுதி). Kural 241 ranks the wealth of grace as the wealth among wealths (அருட்செல்வம் செல்வத்துள் செல்வம்), since goods are found even among the base. Both keep the word செல்வம் and move it from goods to something else: the fire rite in Tirumular, kindness in the Kural.

221 calls the Lord the bright flame who dwells in the heart and is also the cool flame that heads the fire offering (தண்சுடர் ஓமத் தலைவன்). 1565 names him the one whose sign in the Brahmins' Veda is fire (வேதியர் வேதத்து அனற்குறியாளன்) and whose sign is thought. Both read the Vedic fire as a sign of the Lord who also stands within.

source_issues: 217: the verse is obscure throughout and may be corrupt; வேதிரண்டாகி and தாதிரண்டாகிய resist construal.
220: line 3 reads வருஞ்செல்வதது, a misprint for வருஞ்செல்வத்து.
